questions.question: An open pipe has length $L = 0.85\ \mathrm{m}$. Speed of sound $v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Find: (a) the fundamental frequency, (b) the frequency of the 3rd harmonic.
questions.answer:
Open pipe: resonances at $f_n = nv/(2L)$, $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ (all harmonics)

**(a)** $f_1 = \dfrac{v}{2L} = \dfrac{340}{2 \times 0.85} = \dfrac{340}{1.7} = 200\ \mathrm{Hz}$

**(b)** $f_3 = 3f_1 = 600\ \mathrm{Hz}$

questions.question: A closed pipe (open at one end, closed at the other) has length $L = 0.85\ \mathrm{m}$. Speed of sound $v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Find: (a) the fundamental frequency, (b) the first three resonant frequencies.
questions.answer:
Closed pipe: only odd harmonics: $f_n = \dfrac{nv}{4L}$, $n = 1, 3, 5, \ldots$

**(a)** $f_1 = \dfrac{v}{4L} = \dfrac{340}{4 \times 0.85} = \dfrac{340}{3.4} = 100\ \mathrm{Hz}$

**(b)** $f_1 = 100\ \mathrm{Hz}$, $f_3 = 300\ \mathrm{Hz}$, $f_5 = 500\ \mathrm{Hz}$

Note: the fundamental of the closed pipe ($100\ \mathrm{Hz}$) is exactly half that of an open pipe of the same length ($200\ \mathrm{Hz}$).

questions.question: A pipe resonates at consecutive frequencies of $480\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and $640\ \mathrm{Hz}$. Determine whether the pipe is open or closed, and find its fundamental frequency and length. ($v = 320\ \mathrm{m/s}$)
questions.answer:
**Consecutive resonances:**

For an open pipe: $f_n = nf_1$, so consecutive resonances differ by $f_1$: $\Delta f = 640 - 480 = 160\ \mathrm{Hz} = f_1$

For a closed pipe: $\Delta f = 2f_1$ (only odd harmonics, so gap = $2f_1$): $f_1 = 80\ \mathrm{Hz}$, but $480/80 = 6$ (even) — impossible for a closed pipe.

**Open pipe** with $f_1 = 160\ \mathrm{Hz}$:

Check: $480 = 3 \times 160$ ✓, $640 = 4 \times 160$ ✓

**Length:** $L = v/(2f_1) = 320/(2 \times 160) = 1.0\ \mathrm{m}$

questions.question: Explain why a closed pipe (open–closed) produces only odd harmonics, while an open pipe produces all harmonics.
questions.answer:
**Boundary conditions:**

- **Closed end:** Displacement node (air can't move), pressure antinode
- **Open end:** Displacement antinode (air is free), pressure node

**Closed pipe (one end open, one closed):** The pattern must go from node (closed) to antinode (open), requiring an **odd number of quarter-wavelengths** to fit in length $L$:

$L = \dfrac{\lambda}{4}, \dfrac{3\lambda}{4}, \dfrac{5\lambda}{4}, \ldots = \dfrac{(2n-1)\lambda}{4}$

$\Rightarrow f_n = \dfrac{(2n-1)v}{4L}$ — only odd multiples of $f_1$.

**Open pipe (both ends open):** Both ends are antinodes, requiring a **whole number of half-wavelengths**:

$L = \dfrac{n\lambda}{2} \Rightarrow f_n = \dfrac{nv}{2L}$ — all harmonics.

questions.question: A resonance tube (closed bottom, open top) is used to find the speed of sound. The first resonance (fundamental) occurs at $L_1 = 18\ \mathrm{cm}$ and the second resonance at $L_2 = 54\ \mathrm{cm}$ when a tuning fork of $f = 480\ \mathrm{Hz}$ is held at the open end. Find $v$.
questions.answer:
For a closed pipe, resonances at $L = \lambda/4, 3\lambda/4, 5\lambda/4, \ldots$

Consecutive resonances: $L_2 - L_1 = \lambda/2$

$\lambda = 2(L_2 - L_1) = 2(0.54 - 0.18) = 2 \times 0.36 = 0.72\ \mathrm{m}$

$v = f\lambda = 480 \times 0.72 = 345.6 \approx 346\ \mathrm{m/s}$

(The end correction cancels when using $L_2 - L_1$.)

questions.question: An open pipe and a closed pipe have the same fundamental frequency $f_0$. What is the ratio of their lengths $L_{\text{open}}/L_{\text{closed}}$?
questions.answer:
Open pipe fundamental: $f_0 = \dfrac{v}{2L_{\text{open}}}$

Closed pipe fundamental: $f_0 = \dfrac{v}{4L_{\text{closed}}}$

Setting equal:

$\dfrac{v}{2L_{\text{open}}} = \dfrac{v}{4L_{\text{closed}}}$

$L_{\text{open}} = 2L_{\text{closed}}$

$\dfrac{L_{\text{open}}}{L_{\text{closed}}} = 2$

An open pipe must be **twice as long** as a closed pipe to produce the same fundamental frequency.

questions.question: A closed pipe of length $L = 0.4\ \mathrm{m}$ resonates with sound of speed $v = 320\ \mathrm{m/s}$. List the first four resonant frequencies.

A flute is modeled as an open pipe of length $L = 0.66\ \mathrm{m}$. Speed of sound $v = 330\ \mathrm{m/s}$. (a) Find the fundamental frequency. (b) A flute player covers all holes, shortening the effective length to $L' = 0.44\ \mathrm{m}$. Find the new frequency.

A resonance tube experiment: a $500\ \mathrm{Hz}$ tuning fork causes the air column to resonate when $L = 16\ \mathrm{cm}$ (first resonance) and $L = 50\ \mathrm{cm}$ (second resonance). Find: (a) the speed of sound, (b) the end correction $e$ (if first resonance is at $L + e = \lambda/4$).
questions.answer:
**(a)** Difference between consecutive resonances = $\lambda/2$:

$\lambda/2 = 50 - 16 = 34\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.34\ \mathrm{m}$

$\lambda = 0.68\ \mathrm{m}$

$v = f\lambda = 500 \times 0.68 = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$

**(b)** First resonance: $L_1 + e = \lambda/4 = 0.17\ \mathrm{m}$

$e = 0.17 - 0.16 = 0.01\ \mathrm{m} = 1\ \mathrm{cm}$

questions.question: A tube closed at one end is gradually filled with water (decreasing the effective air column length). Starting at $L = 80\ \mathrm{cm}$ with $f = 400\ \mathrm{Hz}$ sound ($v = 320\ \mathrm{m/s}$), find all lengths at which resonance occurs.
questions.answer:
Resonance lengths for closed pipe: $L_n = \dfrac{(2n-1)\lambda}{4}$

$\lambda = v/f = 320/400 = 0.8\ \mathrm{m}$

$L_n = \dfrac{(2n-1) \times 0.8}{4} = (2n-1) \times 0.2\ \mathrm{m}$

$n = 1$: $L = 0.2\ \mathrm{m} = 20\ \mathrm{cm}$ ✓ (within $80\ \mathrm{cm}$)
$n = 2$: $L = 0.6\ \mathrm{m} = 60\ \mathrm{cm}$ ✓
$n = 3$: $L = 1.0\ \mathrm{m}$ ✗ (exceeds $80\ \mathrm{cm}$)

Resonance occurs at $L = 20\ \mathrm{cm}$ and $L = 60\ \mathrm{cm}$.
